rounds.response: Seasonal allergies are your immune system reacting to airborne substances (like tree, grass, or weed pollen or certain molds) that appear at predictable times of year. When those allergens touch cells in your nose and eyes, the immune system triggers release of chemicals (like histamine) that cause blood vessels to swell, nerves to itch, and glands to make extra mucus. That response explains the common pattern: sneezing and a runny nose from irritation and mucus, nasal stuffiness from swollen tissues, and itchy, watery eyes from conjunctival inflammation. Because the offending pollens or molds come and go with the seasons, symptoms often recur at the same time each year.
